summary: **Coram: Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** Application under Sections 14 and Section 15 (1) of Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 15 (1) and Regulation 9 (4) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related matters), Regulations, 2020 for upgradation of inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’. **Parties present:** Shri Kulmani Biswal, Advocate, EPTPL Shri Tabrez Malawat, Advocate, EPTPL Ms. Ankita Bafna, Advocate, EPTPL Shri Syed Hamza, Advocate, EPTPL Ms. Rupali Jain, Advocate, EPTPL Petition for the upgradation of its inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’. 2. By order dated 18.9.2023 in Petition No. 195/TD/2023, Energyedge Power Trading Private Limited was granted a Category ‘V’ trading licence to trade in electricity as an electricity trader in the whole of India, in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related matters), Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020’). 3. The Applicant had approached the Commission for up-gradation of its trading licence from Category ‘V’ to Category ‘IV’ and the Commission, vide Order dated 8.11.2025 in Petition No. 849/TD/2025, up-graded the Category ‘V’ to Category ‘IV’ in accordance with the "Trading Licence Regulations, 2009, subject to the terms and conditions contained in the licence. 4. The Applicant has submitted that in view of the improved market conditions, growth expected in the power market, and looking at future business potential, Energyedge Power Trading Private Limited seeks an up-gradation of its existing trading licence from Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’. The Applicant has submitted that it intends to engage in trading activities up to a quantum of 4,000 MUs annually. The Applicant further stated that its trading volumes have shown a consistent increase over the last financial year, which warrants an upgrade of the category of the licence. The Applicant has further stated that it will make the payment of the applicable licence fee or differential fee for Category III trading licence in terms of the provisions of Regulation 15 (1) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 and will comply with the directions passed by the Commission. 5. The matter was called out for the hearing on 27.8.2026. Learned counsel for the Applicant reiterated the submissions made in the instant Petition and further submitted that the Applicant fulfils all the requirements of Category III inter-State Trading Licence as stipulated in the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, amended from time to time. 6. Vide the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 27.8.2026, the Applicant was directed to submit an Independent Auditor’s Report. 7. The Applicant, vide affidavit dated 2.9.2026, has placed on record the Independent Auditor’s Report. 8. We have considered the submissions of the Applicant. Regulation 9(4) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading License and other Related Matters) Regulations, 2020 (the Trading Licence Regulations 2020) provides as under: _“(4) The Trading Licensee shall make an appropriate application accompanied by prescribed fees for up-gradation of its licence to a higher category or downgradation of its licence to a lower category in order to fulfil the conditions of these regulations in accordance with the procedure specified in Regulation 15 of these regulations.”_ _(a) The Trading Licensee may at any time during a particular year apply for a higher category licence on the basis of the volume proposed to be traded in a particular Year._ _(b) The Trading Licensee shall file an application before the Commission for upgradation of its licence to a higher category as soon as he expects the trading volume to exceed the trading volume limit specified for the Trading Licensee’s existing category._ _(c) The Trading Licensee shall be granted an opportunity of being heard by the Commission before taking a decision on the application_ _(d) The Trading Licensee shall be required to submit the audited special balance sheet to support the compliance of Net Worth requirement for higher category licence._ 10. The Applicant has filed the instant Petition for the upgradation of its inter-State trading licence in accordance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. On perusal of the Petition, the Applicant, being an existing trading licensee, fulfils all technical requirements for the grant of a Category ‘III’ inter-State trading licence. As regards the net worth requirements for Category ‘III”, Regulation 3 (3) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 provides that a person applying for a Category ‘III’ trading licence should have a net worth of Rs. 20 crore and should have maintained a minimum current ratio and liquidity ratio of 1:1 on the date of the Audited Special Balance Sheet accompanying the Petition. 14. In terms of the above, the Applicant meets the net worth, current ratio, and liquidity ratio, requirements specified in the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. Accordingly, we approve the upgradation of the inter-State trading licence of the Applicant from Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’ with effect from the date of issuance of the order. The licensee shall remain bound by the terms and conditions contained in the order dated 18.9.2023 in Petition No. 195/TD/2023, whereby it was issued with Category ‘V’ trading licence. 15. Let an extract copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (Ministry of Power) and the Central Electricity Authority in terms of sub-section (7) of Section 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003, for their information and record.
